boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 4 (119th Congressional Districts), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 4 features for Utah, measured 2026-11-12. These are the districts the current members were elected from in 2024. TIGERweb's layer 0 carries the map for the 120th Congress, whose members were elected on 3 November 2026 and take office on 3 January 2027; measured that day, all 4 differ (the lowest intersection-over-union District 2 at 0.008), and the builder refuses to write layer 4 on or after that date. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: congress-roster.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the public-domain unitedstates/congress-legislators dataset — including each member's district office and Washington office.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 1 (2026 State Legislative Districts - Upper), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 29 features, measured 2026-11-12, which differs from the 2024 vintage (layer 5) only by the Census Bureau's slivers of correction (every intersection-over-union 0.98 or more that day). layers.label: ZIP Code
layers.rank_note: 303 ZIP Code Tabulation Areas that reach into Utah (361 in the app's bounding box), drawn from a tile archive of the ones inside the state; the layer hides outside it

source.answers: The ZIP Code Tabulation Area covering the point — the Census Bureau's areal approximation of the USPS delivery routes sharing a ZIP code, not a postal boundary.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, layer 11 of the PUMA/TAD/TAZ/UGA/ZCTA service, mirrored into a vector-tile archive of the ZCTAs that reach into Utah (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py). ZCTAs carry NO STATE FIELD because they cross state lines, so this is the one TIGERweb layer here fetched by a bounding ENVELOPE rather than STATE='49'. The app's box reaches into Idaho, Wyoming, Colorado, New Mexico, Arizona and Nevada, and measured 2026-11-12, 303 of the 361 ZCTAs in it reach into Utah and are kept in the archive.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a ZIP code is a mail-routing convenience, not a unit of government, so nobody is elected from one. The card says what the boundary actually is rather than leaving a reader to assume it means more.
source.applies: Utah. The layer is hidden outside the state outline, because outside it the Census's point query answers with a neighbouring state's real ZIP code.

layers.label: City or Town
layers.rank_note: 255 incorporated cities and towns, drawn from a tile archive mirrored from TIGERweb

source.answers: The incorporated city or town containing the point, or that the point is outside every one.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places_CouSub_ConCity_SubMCD, layer 4 (incorporated places), mirrored into a vector-tile archive this site serves (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py); 255 records: 152 cities and 103 towns, every one an active government, measured 2026-11-12. MOST OF UTAH IS IN NO INCORPORATED CITY OR TOWN (about 3% of its land, 6,191.6 of 213,921.7 km2, is inside one), and there the county is the general-purpose local government, so an empty card says the point is outside every one rather than naming a place. The Census's census-designated places and county subdivisions are statistical areas with no government and are not drawn.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. No statewide roster of Utah's mayors and councils was read in this pass; the card names the place and links nothing it has not verified. Recorded as gap ut-municipal-officeholders.

layers.label: Tribal Government
layers.rank_note: Tribal land — Utah has 9 pieces, 7 reservations and 2 pieces of off-reservation trust land, held by 7 nations, MEASURED by scripts/build_tribal_areas.py on 2026-11-13, with the counties measured against this app's own county outlines. The largest are the Uintah and Ouray Reservation (17,671.4 km², mostly Duchesne and Uintah counties), the Navajo Nation Reservation (5,188.9 km² in Utah, 8.9% of it, San Juan County), the Goshute Reservation (202.5 km² in Utah, 41.6% of it, Juab County), the Paiute (UT) Reservation (131.2 km²) and the Skull Valley Reservation (72.9 km², Tooele County); the smallest is the Northwestern Shoshone Reservation (0.788 km², Box Elder County). Three pieces cross the state line and are drawn whole: the Navajo Nation, Goshute and Ute Mountain reservations. The Navajo Nation is seated in Arizona and the Ute Mountain Ute Tribe in Colorado. The Census draws tribal subdivisions on the Navajo Nation alone. Ranked after municipalities and before the point layers, as Nevada's and Arizona's are, so they are drawn above the larger areas around them. Drawn although no district is drawn on this land, by Adam's ruling of 2026-09-30: a government answers for that ground, so a reader who clicks it should be told which one.

source.answers: Whether this address is on tribal land, and which nation's government answers for it — Utah has 9 such areas, held by 7 nations: five seated in Utah, the Navajo Nation in Arizona and the Ute Mountain Ute Tribe in Colorado.

boundary.label: US Census Bureau TIGERweb AIANNHA, current vintage — federal reservations and off-reservation trust land, shipped with the app

source.people: No council is named yet. Each nation publishes its own council, and this app has not yet read those pages, so every card says so and links the nation's own site where there is one (ROSTER_NOT_SOUGHT in scripts/build_tribal_areas.py); the councils are to be read and carried one nation at a time. The government, its seat and its website come from the Bureau of Indian Affairs' tribal leaders directory (data/bia-tribal-governments.json), which lists no website for the Skull Valley Band or the Ute Mountain Ute Tribe and no office town for the Confederated Tribes of the Goshute Reservation; for the Goshute the seat is the town the nation's own site gives (Ibapah), and the card says so. The land is joined to the government by this project's own data/tribal-government-join.json.
source.applies: Utah — the 9 pieces of land above. Every other point in the state is on no tribal land the Census draws for a government.

layers.rank_note: nearest police stations by straight-line distance — a point layer, ranked with the other nearest-N layers

source.answers: The three nearest police stations to the point, by straight-line distance, with each one's address.

boundary.label: USGS The National Map — structures layer 53 (Police Stations), queried live at runtime by a bounding envelope through the paged loader. Public domain. Measured 2026-11-12: 156 points in Utah's envelope, which reaches into Idaho, Wyoming, Colorado, New Mexico, Arizona and Nevada; the service caps a page at 2,000 records, so the loader pages if that is ever reached.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a police station is a facility, not an elected district. Nobody is elected from one.
source.applies: Utah — plus the border strip its envelope necessarily includes. A BUILDING, NOT A JURISDICTION: which agency answers at a given point is a service-area question this instance has not been researched for, so the card says where the nearest are and never who serves you. Nearest-three is a proximity fact, so for a reader near the state line the nearest one really may be in a neighbouring state, and the card's intro says these are straight-line distances.

anchor_point.note: Utah State Capitol, 350 State Street, Salt Lake City, Salt Lake County

negative_point.note: Uinta County, Wyoming, north of Evanston and about 12 km east of the Utah line — outside Utah and inside permalink_gate, so the app answers a selection there and every shipped layer correctly returns nothing. Measured 2026-11-12: TIGERweb's state layer names Wyoming here (control: the State Capitol returns Utah), and none of the state's shipped boundary files contains it. WYOMING'S OUTLINE HAS COVERED THIS POINT SINCE THE CHANGE THAT PUBLISHED WYOMING (batch 4 of the state-level launch, written 2026-11-12), which found it inside Wyoming's outline in fleet-outlines.json and no other, AND THE POINT STAYS: measured that day on a 0.05-degree grid, no ground in this app's gate lies more than 2 km from every outline in fleet-outlines.json, so there is nowhere left to move it to. It is still outside Utah and outside every shipped boundary file, which is all the checks that boot on it or select it ask, and a selection the app makes itself never leaves; the click that had to stay here became a Wyoming routing case in the same change, and the click-stays-here check went with it, the way Kentucky's and Tennessee's points stayed put once every neighbour was served.

The 4 U.S. House districts, TIGERweb layer 4 (CD119), the map the sitting members were elected from in 2024, drawn until 3 January 2027.

The ZIP code search index (scripts/build_zip_index.mjs): one Point per ZIP code the app's ZIP layer draws, at the spot inside it on the layer's own ground farthest from every edge, with its extent and its layer, so a ZIP code typed into the search box selects that spot, turns the ZIP layer on and pins it for comparison (ENGINE geocoder-search, showZip). A ZIP code with no spot 75 m clear of every edge is left out, and one that crosses into another app's state is listed by whichever app holds more of it. GENERATED from data/app/tiles/zip-code.pmtiles, with each spot inside metro-outline.json (the outline its coverage test reads); --check rebuilds it from the committed archive and outline. Exact count, because it changes only when the Census Bureau changes its ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, and that wants reading rather than a widened bound.

Utah's tribal land (scripts/build_tribal_areas.py) — 7 reservations and 2 pieces of off-reservation trust land, held by 7 nations, three pieces drawn whole across the state line, simplified by one Douglas-Peucker run at 3 m because the Navajo Nation drawn whole made 2.17 MB (915 KB, 240 KB gzipped; worst stray from the Census's line 3.3 m against a 25 m ceiling). The floor and the ceiling are equal because that is what the Census publishes inside the state on the current vintage, measured 2026-11-13; a change in either direction is a change in the Census's own map and wants reading rather than a widened bound.

The officers Utah elects statewide and its two U.S. senators: state, officers (office, name, the office's own website, the day the name was last checked there) and usSenate. Built weekly by scripts/build_statewide_officials.py from ut/data/source/statewide-officials.source.json, which lists each office, the name and the page that must print it; the build reads robots.txt before every page, refuses to write when a page it read no longer prints the name, keeps the last checked record when a page cannot be read, and takes the senators from senate.gov's own list. Network-first: a name can change.
